Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 14 s. 2023 13 2023 GOV. YVONNE RONA CAGAS Barangay Matti, City of Digos Provincial Government of Davao Del Sur Dear Gov. Cagas: This has reference to your letter dated January 16, 2023 requesting for the Department's action and intervention regarding the impending implementation of the Metro Davao Development Authority (MDDA) as provided under RA No. 11708 on the grounds of its alleged unconstitutionality. The following are the pertinent matters raised in the letter, to wit: (I) The creation of the Special Development and Administrative Region (SDAR) composed of local government units (LGUs) constituting the territorial jurisdiction of MDDA, had no reasonable basis. The LGU classification in the inclusion or exclusion of SDAR did not rest on a reasonable basis and not in line with the purpose of the law. It essentially violated the Equal Protection Clause of the Constitution; (2) The enactment of ordinances by the MDDA binding throughout its territorial jurisdiction will be an encroachment on the legislative powers of the sangguniang bayans, panlungsod and panlalawigan. While there is a proviso in the law that MDDA can only legislate on matters affecting the delivery of "metro-wide services", there is no sufficient and detailed standards on the nature and limits and the MDDA could legislate on purely local matters that are already within the LGU power; (3) The MDDA in the same vein as the MMDA in the case of MMDA vs. Bel Air is not a political unit and cannot legislate ordinances; (4) There were no prior and substantive consultations with the affected LGUs prior to the creation of the MDDA. While the Congress has the power to enact laws, the authors of the law run against Sec. 2, par ( of the Local Government Code. (5) The discretion or initiative to form groups should come from the LGUs, in accordance with Article X, Sec. 132 of the Constitution. development councils is vested with the President and not with the Congress in accordance with Article X, Sec. 143 of the same law. (6) The LGUs part of the SDAR are obliged to share with the MDDA a certain percentage of their National Tax Allotment as determined by the MDDA Council. Such mechanism would deprive the LGU of its property, which in this case refer to public funding, without due process of law and clearly violative of the Constitution; (7) The sangguniang panlalawigan, panlungsod and bayans have no representations in the council; and (8) Flnally, the approval of the MDDA of the LGUs development plans such as investment programming and formulation of plans and programs in the region, undermines the local autonomy of LGUs. At the outset, we would like to thank your good Office for the initiative and that we recognize the concern you have expressed regarding a possible encroachment on the LGU's autonomy. While we affirm that the matter brought before us is in keeping with this Department's mandate over the exercise of general supervision over LGUs, we find that the matter falls beyond this Office's jurisdiction. Considering that the subject matter had already lapsed into a law and is bound for implementation, the matter is beyond this Department's competencies. Moreover, it is beyond the power of this Office to rule on the constitutionality and propriety of the wisdom of our legislators in enacting a law. As to the propriety of seeking redress from the Court, it is best to be guided by the power of judicial review as provided in Article VIII, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution: SECTION 1. The judicial power shall be vested in one Supreme Court and in such lower courts as may be established by law. Judicial power includes the duty of the courts of justice to settle actual controversies involving rights which are legally demandable and enforceable, and to determine whether or not there has been a grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction on the part of any branch or instrumentality of the Government. (Emphasis supplied) As such, courts are not only expected to "settle actual controversies involving rights which are legally demandable and enforceable," but are also empowered to determine if any government branch or instrumentality has acted beyond the scope of its powers, such that there is grave abuse of discretion.4 Nevertheless, our laws allow for judicial remedies to any person whose rights are affected by a statute may bring an action before the trial court to determine its validity through a special civil action of Declaratory Relief, to wit: SECTION I. Who May File Petition. - Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statute, executive order or regulation, ordinance, or any other governmental regulation may, before breach or 3 Section 14. The President shall provide for regional development councils or other similar bodies composed of local govemment officials, regional heads of departments and other government offices, and representatives from non-governmental organizations within the regions for purposes of administrative decentralization to strengthen the autonomy of the units therein and to accelerate the economic and social growth and development of the units in the region. 4 Kilusang Mayo Uno et. al., vs. Hon. Benigno Simeon C. Aquino, et. al., G.R. No. 210500, April 2, 2019. Page 2 of 3

violation thereof, bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder5. In addition, it is settled that the requisites of an action for declaratory relief are: 1] the subject matter of the controversy must be a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, statute, executive order or regulation, or ordinance; 2] the terms of said documents and the validity thereof are doubtful and require judicial construction; 3] there must have been no breach of the documents in question; 4] there must be an actual justiciable controversy or the "ripening seeds" of one between persons whose interests are adverse; 5] the issue must be ripe for judicial determination; and 6] adequate relief is not available through other means or other forms of action or proceeding6. Notwithstanding, we would like to emphasize that this opinion is rendered based solely on the facts you have provided this Department and our appreciation of the same. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter.
